rewrites.title: Single-cell profiling of pre-treatment cells that later survive
rewrites.description: Use barcode-matched sister cells, or live-cell reporters with sorting, to profile the pre-drug transcriptome, chromatin state and signaling of cells that later prove to be survivors. Compare them with matched non-survivors from the same culture to identify factors, such as a drug-efflux or stress-response state, that predate treatment.

rewrites.title: Lineage-barcoded fate mapping before drug exposure
rewrites.description: Tag a clonal population with expressed heritable DNA barcodes, split it into replicate pools, and treat some pools with drug. Sequence survivors and untreated sister pools to test whether persistence is pre-encoded in specific lineages, how many generations it is inherited, and which pre-treatment transcriptional states predict survival. Matching barcodes between sister pools tests whether survivors are pre-existing or drug-induced.

rewrites.title: Fluctuation analysis of published clonal outgrowth data
rewrites.description: Apply fluctuation-test statistics to replicate-well colony counts reported after targeted-drug treatment to estimate the rate at which cells enter the drug-tolerant state. The shape of the across-well count distribution is used to distinguish heritable genetic mutation from reversible epigenetic switching.

rewrites.title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
rewrites.description: Track signaling and cell-cycle reporters (e.g., FUCCI, ERK-KTR, p53 pulses) in individual cells before drug exposure, then map each cell's pre-treatment state to its post-treatment fate. This tests whether survival is predictable from a cell's state at the time of treatment.

rewrites.title: Chromatin accessibility priming with epigenetic perturbation
rewrites.description: Use scATAC-seq on untreated cells to find regions that are already open near survival-associated genes in the rare cells that later persist. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they are causal for tolerance.

rewrites.title: Single-cell apoptotic priming and death timing
rewrites.description: Combine single-cell BH3 profiling or live reporters of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization with time-lapse tracking of death timing across the whole treated population. This tests whether survivors differ in their death execution threshold rather than in drug-pathway signaling, i.e., whether persistence reflects variability in the apoptotic machinery rather than rewiring of the target pathway.

rewrites.title: Automated detection and isolation of rare dividing cells under drug
rewrites.description: Continuously image millions of drug-treated cells and automatically flag the rare cells that are still dividing or re-entering the cell cycle. Photoconvert or photo-tag only those cells and isolate them immediately for scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteomics. This profiles the actual survivors as they diverge from the rest of the population, instead of using bulk measurements or post-hoc resistant lines.

rewrites.title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
rewrites.description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming in each cell before drug exposure (BH3 profiling by flow cytometry, with cytochrome c release after BH3 peptides), then sort high- and low-priming subpopulations and compare their survival under the drug. If priming predicts survival, test whether BH3 mimetics that push low-priming cells toward death eliminate the survivors.

rewrites.title: Mother-daughter inheritance of protein aggregates
rewrites.description: Express an aggregation-prone fluorescent reporter or an HSP70 chaperone sensor, then track mother-daughter pairs through mitosis during drug exposure. Test whether daughters that inherit a low aggregate or damaged-protein burden are the ones that survive, which would indicate that persistence reflects asymmetric inheritance of proteostatic burden rather than a fixed transcriptional state.

rewrites.title: Neighbor ablation to test the role of the local niche
rewrites.description: Image survival in situ without replating, and record each cell's local density and neighbor identity. Test causality by selectively killing or silencing defined neighbor subsets (inducible caspase or optogenetic ablation in a mixed co-culture) and by transferring conditioned medium from candidate protective neighborhoods. This tests whether survival is conferred by the local niche rather than by the cell's intrinsic state, going beyond correlational spatial description.

rewrites.title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
rewrites.description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into parallel replicate cultures, and treat with the drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, resistance is a pre-existing, heritable state. If different barcodes survive in each replicate, it is a stochastic, transient state. The variance in survivor numbers across replicates distinguishes the two models and gives switching rates.

rewrites.title: Live-cell signaling and cell-cycle reporters linked to fate
rewrites.description: Express biosensors such as ERK or AKT kinase translocation reporters and FUCCI cell-cycle markers, then image individual cells continuously through drug addition and record their fate. Correlate signaling amplitude, dynamics, and cell-cycle phase at the time of treatment with eventual survival to identify dynamic states that predict persistence.

rewrites.title: Spatially resolved transcriptomics of rare survivors in situ
rewrites.description: Apply in situ sequencing or multiplexed single-molecule FISH to the treated monolayer on fixed plates without dissociating cells, so that rare persisters are measured together with their immediate neighbors and their position in the colony. This tests whether survival is driven by cell-intrinsic state or by local microenvironment effects such as crowding, paracrine signaling, and nutrient gradients.

rewrites.title: Membrane potential sorting with ion-channel perturbation
rewrites.description: Stain live cells with voltage-sensitive dyes to measure resting membrane potential, sort the hyperpolarized and depolarized fractions, and re-challenge each with the drug. Then test whether pharmacological or genetic changes to specific K+ or Cl- channels shift the survival fraction, which would indicate a bioelectric state that predisposes cells to tolerance.

rewrites.title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D culture or xenografts
rewrites.description: Run spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging (such as CODEX) on drug-treated spheroids or tumors, and test whether survivors cluster by local oxygen, density, stromal contact, or neighbor-secreted signals. Complement this with conditioned-medium and density-titration experiments to determine whether tolerance is cell-intrinsic or induced by neighbors.

rewrites.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens plus BH3 profiling
rewrites.description: Run CRISPR knockout/activation screens under drug to identify genes that set the persister fraction, and pair them with single-cell BH3 profiling to test whether survivors are in a lower apoptotic-priming state. This separates causal drivers from correlates and shows whether survival works through apoptosis evasion, metabolism, or stress response.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling of persisters over time
rewrites.description: Run scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq on cells before treatment, during drug exposure, and after regrowth. This can identify persister-specific transcriptional programs, such as drug-efflux, stress-response, or dedifferentiated states, along with their regulatory chromatin changes.

rewrites.title: Tracking asymmetric partitioning at division
rewrites.description: Pulse-label mitochondria, aggregated proteins, or the drug target using photoconvertible or SNAP-tag chemistry. Follow how these components are split between daughter cells in the divisions before treatment, and test whether daughters that inherit an unequal share are the ones that later survive the drug.

rewrites.title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
rewrites.description: Micropattern or seed cells at defined local densities, image the full field during treatment, and model each cell's survival as a function of its own state versus the number, proximity, and death timing of its neighbors. Complement this with conditioned-medium and apoptotic-debris transfer experiments. This tests whether survival is cell-autonomous or depends on the local microenvironment and signals from dying neighbors.

rewrites.title: Live imaging of a primed-state reporter linked to later sequencing
rewrites.description: Continuously image cells carrying a reporter for the candidate primed state (e.g., a knock-in of a resistance-associated gene) from before drug addition through outcome, then retrieve individual cells for sequencing via in situ transcriptomics or Live-seq. This reveals whether the state pre-exists, how fast it fluctuates relative to the treatment window, and whether survivors were already in the state at t=0 or entered it stochastically afterward, which destructive snapshot measurements cannot distinguish.
